method: Manual inspection of the top-1 delivered result per arm, from the stored title and URL. The label is about whether the page can answer the asked question, not whether it mentions the entity. One auditor, 31 cases x 5 arms, 155 rows; every row can be re-derived from the capture.

labels.answer: a guide / release / comparison / documentation page that is expected to contain the specific answer
labels.topic_only: topically correct (official homepage, portal, docs index) but carrying no specific answer
labels.wrong: unrelated, a dictionary or encyclopedia entry for a single word, a mirror or a fan site

why_manual: The keyword rule saturates on a 12-row pool: a random draw of six rows already 'hits' in 0.96 (loose rule) / 0.56 (strict rule) of cases, so it cannot rank the arms. The manual label is a judgement, not a truth oracle, and it is unblinded and single-auditor; it is used because it is the only signal here that separates a homepage from a page that answers.

arms.A: production fallback: SearXNG first, then Bing, then DDG (31/31 answered by SearXNG)
arms.B: merge, Bing pool first, no rerank
arms.D: merge, DuckDuckGo pool first, no rerank
arms.C_prod: merge + production _rank_merged (assess_sources on the planned query)
